result:
The final answer r/(r+1) is correct, and the proposed argument holds up.

**Setup.** Writing each S-smooth number as its exponent vector turns the forbidden set {n, p₁n, …, p_r n} into a translate a+V, where V = {0, e₁, …, e_r}. So F_S(X) is the largest subset of the simplex T_X containing no full translate of V.

**Upper bound.**
- Stars a+V ⊆ T_X are exactly those with a ∈ T_{X/P}, where P = max p_i. Their number is Ψ_S(X/P) = (1+o(1))Ψ_S(X), because Ψ_S grows like (log X)^r.
- Every such star must contain a point of the complement B = T_X \ A.
- Each point of B lies in at most r+1 stars (once as the base point, once as each of the r tips).
- Hence |B| ≥ (1+o(1))N/(r+1), so |A| ≤ (r/(r+1)+o(1))N.

**Construction.**
- Define φ(a) = Σ i·a_i mod (r+1).
- On V the values are 0, 1, …, r, so φ maps V bijectively onto ℤ/(r+1).
- Every translate a+V therefore contains exactly one point with φ ≡ 0.
- Removing all points with φ ≡ 0 leaves a set with no full star.
- The removed points form one coset of an index-(r+1) sublattice. That coset has (1+o(1))N/(r+1) points in the dilating simplex.
- So |A| = (r/(r+1)+o(1))N.

**Checks.** For r = 1, avoiding {n, pn} gives density 1/2, matching r/(r+1). For S = {2,3}, avoiding {n, 2n, 3n} gives density 2/3 via the 3-coloring a+2b mod 3, also matching.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
